subject: Next steps: hosting decision roadmap & legacy LLM exit plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@stratusretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + suggested hosting decision roadmap

Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. I pulled together a short recap and a proposed decision roadmap so we can converge on the right hosting mode for Stratus Retail. High-level notes:

- Current environment: mix of OpenAI API usage (text+embeddings) for customer chat, and an internal legacy GPU cluster (TF1/Caffe) used for offline reranking.
- Primary goals: reduce token spend, meet <200ms median response for customer chat, and strict data isolation for PII (SOC2 / VPC requirement).
- Migration drivers: end-of-life support for legacy cluster, desire to consolidate inference billing and telemetry, and regulatory audits next quarter.

Suggested hosting decision roadmap (short):
1) Short POC (2 weeks): run a representative traffic slice against Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with quantized model variants to verify latency & unit cost.
2) Security gating (1 week): run quick network checklist for Private VPC + KMS/HSM compatibility and provide evidence for your infosec team.
3) Cutover decision (1–2 weeks after POC): if telemetry and SLOs meet requirements, schedule Dedicated -> Dedicated Reserved; if VPC/KMS is hard requirement, pivot to Private deployment.

Action items / asks from your side to scope the POC:
- Typical concurrent requests at peak and expected throughput percentage to test (e.g., 30rps).
- Representative prompt shapes and average sequence length (tokens).
- Approx size of embeddings corpus (GB) and whether you require on-prem storage for vectors.
- Any immediate redlines from legal/infosec (IP retention, encryption at rest with HSM)

Attachments: redwood-map-v1.pdf (high-level roadmap), SOW-draft-v0.9.pdf (placeholder SOW), network-diagram-stub.png (we sketched an example VPC layout).

Proposed next step: brief mutual action plan meeting Thursday to confirm evaluation traffic and sign off access for the POC. Karthik — can you lead the Dedicated configuration? Marissa — we may need CS for cutover notes.

Thanks,
Rishi
---
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-map-v1.pdf (summary), SOW-draft-v0.9.pdf (SOW stub)
From: Samira Khan <skhan@stratusretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Stratus Retail Security <infosec@stratusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested hosting decision roadmap

Rishi — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Infrastructure: our legacy cluster handles overnight reranking and some custom models that aren’t going to be migrated immediately. We need a plan to keep parity for the reranker outputs during transition.
- Security: infosec flagged that we must have customer data segmented by tenant and keys under our KMS (HSM preferred). If Redwood’s Private VPC supports customer-managed KMS and we can keep vectors out of the public cloud, that will be ideal.
- Latency: 200ms median is right, 95th should not exceed 400ms for chat requests.
- Cost/levers: we need a sense of quantization and batching tradeoffs you’ll test during the POC and how they affect quality.

Questions:
1) If the POC runs on Dedicated and we like the performance but infosec wants HSM + customer-managed keys, is the migration from Dedicated -> Private straightforward? What’s the expected timeline and downtime?
2) Can you demonstrate rollback/fallback to OpenAI APIs during the POC if there are quality regressions?

We’re available Thursday 10am PT for the MAP meeting. I’ll loop back with infosec on any hard redlines before then.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Engineering | Stratus Retail
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@stratusretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested hosting decision roadmap

Samira — great questions, answered inline below.

1) Dedicated -> Private migration: straightforward in our playbook, but timeline depends on networking approvals. Typical path: export model artifacts + KV cache warmup -> provision Private control plane + customer VPC peering -> cut traffic (canary) -> final switch. Total calendar time: usually 2–4 weeks; downtime can be zero if canary routing is used. We’ll provide a checklist for your infra team.

2) Fallbacks and rollback: yes — during the POC we can route a percentage of traffic to OpenAI (or your existing API keys) as a quality safety net and compare outputs. We’ll record metrics and an automatic fallback policy if quality drops.

POC test matrix we’ll run (summary):
- Latency: median & 95th with representative traffic at 30/60/120 rps slices.
- Cost: per-token unit cost with baseline (OpenAI) and Redwood quantized models.
- Quality: A/B evals on 500 sample prompts and embeddings recall on a 200k-sample subset.
- Security: network connectivity test + KMS integration + evidence pack for SOC2 questionnaire.

Next steps (agreed):
- Thursday 10am PT: MAP meeting to confirm traffic and sign off POC scope (Karthik to own Dedicated setup).
- I’ll share a short access checklist for your infra and a lightweight test script for the sample prompts.

Attachments: updated SOW stub (SOW-draft-v0.9.pdf) for review.

Regards,
Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Stratus MAP and migration notes

Quick internal note after Samira’s reply — capture the internal asks and owners here so we don’t lose track:

- Karthik: prepare a Dedicated pool config (GPUs + burst policy) and an autoscale plan. Include an option to export model artifacts for Private. Target: 2d delivery before Thursday call.
- Rishi: draft the short access checklist for Stratus infra (VPC peering, CIDR ranges, KMS, service accounts).
- Marissa (CS): prepare cutover runbook templates and rollback steps; include monitoring/alert thresholds for 95th latency and error rates.
- Legal/Product: review SOW-draft-v0.9.pdf for any immediate redlines (billing, data retention).

I’ll join the Thursday 10am PT call to own cutover comms.

-Marissa
